hints: Look closely at the pore size, only $2.4\text{ nm}$ in diameter, just big enough to let tiny glucose molecules through. Ask yourself if any of 1 to 4 are that tiny or much bigger.

Remember the rule for partial permeability: only particles smaller than the pore can diffuse through. Think about the real size of a whole bacterium, a protein like haemoglobin, a ribosome and a large polysaccharide like glycogen.
walkthrough:
**Understand what the pore allows**

Visking tubing acts like a sieve. Small molecules like glucose (less than $1\text{ nm}$ across) can fit through the $2.4\text{ nm}$ pores.

Anything larger than $2.4\text{ nm}$ is held back.

**Compare the sizes of 1 to 4**

All four are huge compared to glucose. Bacteria are whole cells, about $1000\text{ nm}$ or more long.

Haemoglobin is a globular protein about $5.5\text{ nm}$ in diameter, ribosomes are about $20\text{ nm}$ in diameter, and glycogen is a very large branched polysaccharide.

**Make the decision**

Since $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ are all larger than $2.4\text{ nm}$, none of them can fit through the pores. That means the answer is none of the above.

options.A: Incorrect. Bacteria (cells) and ribosomes (about $20\text{ nm}$) are both far larger than the $2.4\text{ nm}$ pore.
options.B: Incorrect. Haemoglobin (about $5.5\text{ nm}$) and glycogen (a huge polysaccharide) are both too large to pass through.
options.C: Incorrect. Haemoglobin alone is still larger than $2.4\text{ nm}$, so it cannot diffuse through.
options.D: Correct. All four structures are larger than the pore size, so none of them can pass through.
